The compiled API imports the workspace package by name, but the package export resolves to raw TypeScript instead of emitted JavaScript.

interpretation: This confirms the scratch API TypeScript build succeeds and that build-then-prune removes the four advisory-related packages while retaining Prisma Client, its PostgreSQL adapter, and pg.
It does not validate the complete deployed API runtime or a database request because startup fails on the workspace package export before opening an HTTP listener.
The previous narrower scratch smoke that imported the generated client and constructed PrismaClient/PrismaPg without connecting remains valid; it is not API startup or query evidence.
limits: PGlite is not PostgreSQL and this setup does not prove PostgreSQL MVCC, row locks, rollback, durability, migrations through Prisma Migrate, or multi-instance behavior.
No production database, network connection, or live deployment artifact was used.
The attempt did not apply a scratch-only export rewrite or bundler workaround, so it preserves the observed runtime packaging blocker.
Any claim about current published advisory ranges or fixed upstream Prisma pins requires up-to-date external source verification; this file records the local locked-tree experiment only.
